title-proc.eng: Scientific e-journals and e-books: subscription, access and related services

description-proc.eng: The need for a dedicated tender arises from the increasingly central role of scientific knowledge in law enforcement training, research, and practice. Policing and security are no longer shaped only by professional experience or internal doctrine, but also by empirical research, data analysis, and interdisciplinary evidence. Access to peer-reviewed academic publications is therefore essential to ensure that training content, analytical work, and operational methodologies are informed by reliable, current, and validated knowledge. Without a formal procurement mechanism, access to such resources would remain fragmented, uneven, and dependent on ad hoc arrangements, creating a risk that parts of the community rely on incomplete or outdated information. A dedicated tender is therefore necessary to secure stable, lawful, and comprehensive access to high-quality scientific e-journals and e-books across the CEPOL community. The tender is also needed to ensure equal and organised access for all relevant users, including trainers, analysts, researchers, and operational staff. In the absence of a structured contractual framework, access to scientific literature is likely to vary between institutions and individuals, undermining consistency in training delivery, limiting the dissemination of best practices, and reducing the overall coherence of professional development across jurisdictions. Centralised procurement will support a common knowledge base, strengthen harmonisation in law enforcement education, and reinforce CEPOL’s role as a hub for knowledge exchange and evidence-based learning. Finally, the tender is necessary to address the technical and economic specificities of accessing licensed academic content in a controlled, sustainable, and cost-effective manner. Scientific publishers generally rely on specific licensing, authentication, and access-management systems, which must be compatible with CEPOL’s existing digital environment. Without a procurement procedure tailored to these requirements, there is a significant risk of selecting solutions that are technically unsuitable, financially inefficient, or dependent on costly bespoke development. By defining clear technical requirements and prioritising solutions that can be implemented within the existing environment, the tender ensures operational feasibility, protects institutional resources, and guarantees continuity and reliability of access to essential scientific knowledge.

Dit betreft o.a. toestellen voor de meting van besmetting (d.i. lucht, oppervlakte, personen, wipes, … ), toestellen voor dosistempometingen (d.i. gamma, neutronen, spectroscopisch, hoog-en laag meetbereik, … ), toestellen voor Radon en Tritium metingen, actieve dosismeters, en controle-en kalibratiebronnen. Er wordt voorzien in het opzetten van een lange termijn dynamisch aankoopsysteem, ingedeeld in diverse categorieën (zoals bijvoorbeeld besmettingsmonitoren, dosismeters, enz) op grond waarvan de latere deelopdrachten kunnen worden geplaatst. Middels het dynamisch aankoopsysteem wenst de aanbestedende overheid een open bestand van ondernemers die voldoen aan de selectiecriteria en tot het systeem zijn toegelaten samen te stellen, die in staat zijn deze toestellen te leveren en te onderhouden. Er kunnen gedurende de volledige looptijd van het dynamisch aankoopsysteem aanvragen tot deelneming worden ingediend, op grond waarvan nieuwe ondernemers, indien zij voldoen aan de selectiecriteria, kunnen worden toegelaten tot het dynamisch aankoopsysteem. Alle tot een bepaalde categorie toegelaten deelnemers, en enkel deze deelnemers, worden in het kader van het dynamisch aankoopsysteem op geregelde tijdstippen uitgenodigd om een offerte in te dienen voor een specifieke leveringsopdracht (“deelopdracht”). Deze deelopdrachten worden gegund volgens de regels van de niet-openbare procedure, zoals van toepassing in het kader van een dynamisch aankoopsysteem (cfr. artikel 44 Overheidsopdrachtenwet en de artikelen 101 e.v. KB Plaatsing), waarbij alle toegelaten deelnemers verplicht in mededinging worden gesteld. De procedure van het dynamisch aankoopsysteem (afkorting D.A.S.), zoals voorzien in artikel 44 van de Wet Overheidsopdrachten, lijkt de meest geschikte procedure te zijn voor deze opdracht, aangezien: • het betrekking heeft op leveringen van courant gebruik die algemeen beschikbaar zijn op de markt. • dit systeem de mogelijkheid biedt om voor lange termijn (bvb. 10 jaar) een open bestand van ondernemers te beheren die voldoen aan de selectiecriteria, waarbij ondernemers zich op elk moment kunnen aanmelden en, indien zij voldoen aan deze criteria, tot het systeem worden toegelaten. • overeenkomstig artikel 44, §2 van de Wet Overheidsopdrachten, alle ondernemers die aan de selectiecriteria voldoen tot het systeem worden toegelaten, zonder beperking in aantal; voor elke specifieke opdracht, overeenkomstig artikel 103 van het koninklijk besluit Plaatsing, alle toegelaten deelnemers (of deze binnen de relevante categorie) verplicht worden uitgenodigd om een offerte in te dienen, waardoor de mededinging wordt gewaarborgd. • het systeem kan worden ingedeeld in categorieën (bijvoorbeeld per type toestel), waardoor per specifieke opdracht gericht mededinging kan worden georganiseerd tussen de relevante deelnemers. • het systeem aldus flexibiliteit biedt om per specifieke opdracht de technische specificaties en uitvoeringsvoorwaarden nader te bepalen. description-proc.eng: Radio monitoring: measuring devices for operational nuclear safety in a nuclear plant. These include devices for measuring contamination (i.e. air, surface, people, wipes, etc.), devices for dose rate measurements (i.e. gamma, neutrons, spectroscopic, high and low measurement range, etc.), devices for radon and tritium measurements, active dosimeters, and control and calibration sources. A long-term Dynamic Purchasing System will be set up. This will be divided into several categories (such as, for example, contamination monitors, dosimeters, etc.), based on which partial contracts can be placed later on. Through the Dynamic Purchasing System, the Awarding Authority wishes to create an open pool of entrepreneurs that meet the selection criteria and have been admitted to the system, who are able to supply and maintain these devices. Requests to participate may be made throughout the entire duration of the Dynamic Purchasing System, on the basis of which new entrepreneurs may be admitted to the Dynamic Purchasing System, provided they meet the selection criteria. All participants admitted to a given category, and only those participants, will be invited at regular intervals under the Dynamic Purchasing System to submit a tender for a specific supply contract ("partial contract"). These partial contracts will be awarded according to the rules of the restricted procedure, as applicable under a Dynamic Purchasing System (in accordance with Article 44 of the Public Contracts Act and Articles 101 et seq. of the Royal Decree on the award of public contracts), in which all participants will be placed in competition. The procedure of the Dynamic Purchasing System (abbreviated as D.P.S.), as provided for by Article 44 of the Public Contracts Act, seems to be the most suitable procedure for this contract, given that: • it relates to commonly used supplies that are generally available on the market; • this system offers the possibility of managing an open pool of entrepreneurs that meet the selection criteria in the long term (e.g. for 10 years), allowing entrepreneurs to register at any time for admission to the system, provided they meet these criteria; • in accordance with Article 44, §2 of the Public Contracts Act, all entrepreneurs that meet the selection criteria are admitted to the system, without any limit in number; for each specific contract, in accordance with Article 103 of the Royal Decree on the award of public contracts, all admitted participants (or those within the relevant category) are obliged to submit a tender, which ensures competition; • the system can be divided into categories (e.g. per type of device), allowing for a specific competition to be organised between the relevant participants for each specific contract; • thus, the system offers flexibility to determine the detailed technical specifications and conditions of performance for each specific contract. description-proc.eng: The project Mobilité Verte au Sénégal (MoVe Senegal) is implemented by the Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH, in partnership with the Senegalese Ministry of Land and Air Transports, (MiTTA) which is the political counterpart, and the Executive Council for Sustainable Urban Transportation (CETUD) being the implementing partner. MoVe Senegal is commissioned by the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ). The project is part of the development cooperation programme "Sustainable Energy Supply and Urban Development in Senegal", which aims to make cities sustainable, climate-neutral, resilient and liveable. MoVe Senegal is in line with Senegal National Development Strategy 2025-2029, which is a strategy for implementing its Vision 2050. Senegal's climate protection targets, set out in the Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs), provide for a reduction in greenhouse gas emissions by 23% and 29% (subject to external support) by 2030. In Senegal, the transport sector accounts for 64% of fossil fuel consumption and thus also the largest share of the associated greenhouse gas emissions. The majority of transport demand is generated in the Dakar metropolitan area with 3.9 million inhabitants. According to forecasts from the city"s Sustainable Urban Mobility Plan (Plan de Mobilité Urbaine Durable, PMUD), transport demand in the centre of Dakar will increase by 40% by 2035. On the outskirts, demand is expected to increase fivefold compared to 2019. In Dakar, 69% of journeys are made on foot. However, pedestrians face considerable dangers because sidewalks and crossings are often poorly planned, dilapidated, or non-existent. Over 60% of road users complain about the lack of sidewalks or their obstruction by parked cars, mobile traders, shops, and informal public transport stops. Only around 1% of journeys in Dakar are made by bicycle, despite its widespread use in other cities in the country. The lack of infrastructure, disregard for traffic rules by motorists, high risk of bicycle theft, and obstructions caused by parking and stalls make cycling extremely dangerous in Dakar. 90% of men, but only 36% of women, can ride a bicycle and only 15% of the residents have a bicycle. Overall, the city lacks a coherent strategy for active modes of transport that aims to integrate walking and cycling into the urban transport system. Therefore, project"s primary objective is to anchor active mobility as an integral component of transport planning in the Dakar metropolitan region. It is structured in 3 outputs: - Output 1 focuses on strategies and coordination. Within this output a Steering Committee for Active Mobility will be supported, a strategy for walking and cycling will be prepared and action plans for the improvement of active mobility in the Dakar Metropolitan Region will be developed. - Output 2 aims to strengthen the technical competences of technical experts to improve pedestrian access to public transport in the Dakar metropolitan region. In this output a Green Corridor to improve pedestrian access to public transport will be prepared with the public administrations of the Dakar metropolitan region, based on a participation process. - Output 3 focuses on increasing the use of bicycles among pupils and students in the Dakar metropolitan region. To this end, a bike sharing system will be developed on the campus of the Université Cheikh Anta Diop de Dakar (UCAD) together with CETUD and the university administration. This includes the identification of a suitable business model, the implementing of the bike sharing system and the development of plans to connect the campus to the public transport system using active modes.

title-proc.eng: The collection, transportation and treatment of bio waste.

description-proc.eng: The Contracting Authority Avfall Sør Husholdning AS is a part of Avfall Sør konsern, which is owned 100% by Kristiansand and Vennesla municipalities in Agder. The company provides waste and sanitation services to all inhabitants in the owner municipalities and serves approx. 55,500 residential units with dunk sanitation, 5,000 residential units with buried systems and 3,700 cabin subscribers. In addition, the company operates three recycling stations and a large waste facility at Støleheia with various treatment activities such as sorting, composting, tiling and depositing. Avfall Sør Husholdning AS is the contracting authority for this competition. Read more about Avfall Sør at: www.avfallsor.no Background Avfall Sør Husholdning AS is currently collecting food and bio waste from households in the owner municipalities. The waste is transported to Støleheia, where it is composted in a separate facility. The finished compost is to be refined to soil products that are traded for various purpose. From 1 September the new supplier will take over the collection of household waste on behalf of the contracting authority. The collection routes are thus altered and the collection frequency for food and bio-waste is changed from weekly to collection every two weeks. The change is a part of Avfall Sør ́s work with increasing the sorting of food and bio waste. Analyses show that there are still significant amounts of food waste in the residue waste, and the aim is to move a greater share of this to the bio-waste scheme. At the same time, garden and park waste makes up a significant part of the total amount of bio-waste. In 2025, this fraction accounted for about 20 percent of the total tonnage. Avfall Sør also handles municipal commercial waste on behalf of the owner municipalities. This waste flow is mainly equivalent to composition and quality as bio-waste from households, but normally contains a lower portion of garden and park waste. The new manure products regulation, which came into force in 2025, sets strict requirements for businesses that produce natural fertiliser products of organic origin. Amongst other things, the requirements for quality assurance, documentation, traceability, internal control and product responsibility have been strengthened. Fulfilment of these requirements would require considerable investments in infrastructure, process installations, quality systems and further development of the composting facility. After a combined assessment of investment needs, operational finances, regulation requirements and future treatment systems, Avfall Sør Husholdning AS has therefore decided to discontinue separate composting of bio waste. Instead, the collection, transport and treatment of the bio-waste will be outsourced so that the waste can be treated at an external facility with the necessary capacity and competence to meet the current requirements. This solution is considered the most cost efficient and robust in the long term, while ensuring that bio-waste is treated in accordance with current regulations and can be utilised as a valuable circular resource. Description of the assignment The contracting authority needs a robust and environmentally responsible system for handling bio-waste (food and garden/park), from households and business customers. The procurement shall ensure continuity in the receipt, transport and treatment of waste, and contribute to the waste being used as a resource through material recovery and/or energy recovery. The aim of the procurement is to establish a contract with a tenderer who can safeguard the entire value chain from collection at the contracting authority ́s waste facility at Støleheia, until final treatment. The system shall support the contracting authority ́s work on sustainable waste management in the region around Kristiansand and contribute to predictable operation in the contract period. The procurement is particularly important in order to ensure sufficient treatment capacity, stable logistics and a system that fulfils the current environmental requirements as well as requirements for proper handling of the bio waste. The contracting authority may also receive and process bio-waste from both households and commercial customers on behalf of other municipalities in the region around us. These volumes will then be able to flow to this contract and are taken into consideration in the competition ́s value limitations. The contract will be valid for 1 year, with an option for the contracting authority to extend the contract for 1 year at a time for up to 3 years, so that the maximum total contract period is 4 years.

In the context of current geopolitical developments, access to cost-competitive green hydrogen derivatives constitutes a strategic interest for Germany and the European Union. To strengthen India"s developing hydrogen ecosystem offers a relevant framework for engagement by German companies across the hydrogen value chain and contributes to strengthening sustainable economic cooperation. The Project has the following Outputs: - Output 1 Indian public institutions have recommendations based on international experience for the implementation of India's hydrogen strategy. - Output 2 Companies and associations now have improved decision-making bases for the use of green hydrogen in industrial sectors that are difficult to electrify. - Output 3 The conditions for gender-equitable participation of actors from politics, business, science and civil society in the Indian green hydrogen economy have improved.

During transport and processing, the wafers are mechanically touched only at the wafer edge, and they can be flipped in vacuum between the processes. The object of the tender process and the technical requirements are described in more detail in the invitation to tender documents.
